title: Dashboard ghost tiles and span-index race causing intermittent tenant metric blackout
creator: Ethan Morales
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported dashboards showing stale or empty tiles during autoscaling events and a sequence of related tracing gaps. Affected tenants include Hosted customers and several Dedicated/Private deployments. Symptoms were: dashboard widgets returning 'no data', live panels blanking for 1–8 minutes, and missing span-to-metric stitching in traces. This ticket tracks identification, hotfix rollout, and validation across all deployment modes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hotfix deployed to hosted and dedicated with verification runbooks documented.
- Private customers provided patch and upgrade guidance.
- Observability restores show continuous span-to-metric links for 48h at production load.
- Postmortem created, RCA validated by SRE and product, follow-ups scheduled.
root_cause_summary: During aggressive autoscale/drain cycles, the telemetry ingestion pipeline evicted metric shards before pending span-index compaction tasks completed. A race between shard eviction and the span-to-metric stitcher produced transient index holes (shadowed spans) and time-window aliasing that caused dashboard query planners to omit affected series. Additionally, a recent optimization that aggressively trimmed per-tenant in-memory indexes exacerbated the windowing skew on Dedicated hosts, and Private deployments running older compaction agents were vulnerable to longer repair windows.
mitigation_plan:
1) Immediate: deploy ingestion gate that delays shard eviction until compaction snapshot confirms completion (hosted roll).
2) Hotfix: adjust shard-eviction TTL from 30s to 5m for at-risk tenants and enable a temporary background reindex sweep.
3) Monitoring: add a real-time "pending-compaction" metric and dashboard with alerts on backlog > 0.
4) Dedicated/Private: ship agent update with compaction backoff and provide assisted upgrade for customers reporting gaps.
5) Long-term: revisit compaction windowing and add stronger transactional handoff between index writer and eviction manager.
rollback_plan: If hotfix causes unexpected memory pressure or increased ingestion lag: 1) revert eviction TTL to previous value via feature flag (config service), 2) disable reindex sweep, 3) reduce throughput via temporary rate-limits and notify affected customers. Rollback steps are automated in the runbook and tested with canary tenant beforehand.

notes: Design trade-off: increasing eviction TTL increases memory footprint and may delay reclaim during noisy neighbors — mitigated by background sweep and canary gating.
Action item: Product to review SLA implications for Dedicated tenants if retention of in-memory indexes is extended.
Follow-up: schedule deep-dive with storage and kernel-selection teams to explore transactional handoff; target Cycle 2026-W15.
QA: add regression test that simulates compaction + eviction race with variable network delays to CI matrix.
